sourceProfiles.notInstalled: No AWS SDK is a dependency. The adapter speaks the documented JSON wire format directly with fetch and zod.
No Vercel SDK or CLI is a dependency. The device grant is the generic RFC 8628 family under an issuer policy; the two REST reads are plain fetch calls validated with zod.

limitations: Live account evidence blocked: no authorized AWS account or IAM Identity Center instance exists in this environment, so the sign-in has never run against AWS

The Portal API host (portal.sso.<region>.amazonaws.com), the unit of RoleCredentials.expiration, how slow_down grows the interval, which error answers a wrong or used deviceCode, and when a refresh token is issued are assumptions listed in AWS_ASSUMPTIONS; the double serves them as written there
Identity is the portal's report for the sign-in; STS GetCallerIdentity is not called, so the account the credentials act in is not independently observed
Logout ends the sign-in session; role sessions already issued continue until their own expiry, so an upstream disconnect never claims to end them

Authorization-code with PKCE for IAM Identity Center is not implemented: RegisterClient supports it, but a second browser leg adds nothing the device grant does not for a host that has no redirect origin of its own
workItems.notes: The person signs in on the AWS access portal's own page; the adapter registers a public client per sign-in, shows the verification URI and user code through the same device-code handoff every device grant here issues, polls CreateToken (pending, slow_down, access_denied, expired_token, a lost response) with each poll journaled before it is sent, then lists the accounts the binding permits and either binds the one account and role there is or asks the person. GetRoleCredentials issues the role's credentials, which go into custody with the sign-in tokens as one record so a local disconnect releases all of it. Role credentials are renewed with a new GetRoleCredentials call while the access token holds; only a lapsed access token costs a refresh grant, which is presented once.

limitations: Live account evidence blocked: no authorized Vercel account, team or Sign in with Vercel application exists in this environment, so the sign-in has never run against Vercel

No page describes the device authorization endpoint, so its request and response, the verification page, that a dashboard-made application may use the device grant, that a `none` client is accepted there, the error codes for a replayed code or refresh token, and that teams page by `until` are assumptions listed in VERCEL_ACCOUNT_ASSUMPTIONS; the double serves them as written there
That Vercel Connect accepts a sign-in token as its management credential is unverified: the permissions page calls API permissions a private beta, and the Connect double models the acceptance

The recorded discovery document lists no `none` client authentication method, so RFC 7591 registration of a public client is refused by the generic client resolution; the host's client is pre-registered

The sign-in token is the person's own: Vercel reports granted scopes, not the permissions the person holds in the team, and the team binding narrows what this connection is for, not what the token can do
Authorization code with PKCE (Sign in with Vercel) is a documented non-goal here: it is the generic authorization-code family under another issuer policy, not a second mechanism

The shipping server does not compose the two connections: a host that wants the sign-in to feed the Connect management leg passes `vercelManagementToken` (see accountManagementSource) and owns the lookup of the person's connection
workItems.notes: The person signs in on Vercel's own page with the generic device-code handoff; the adapter then reads who signed in (GET /v2/user) and which teams they belong to (GET /v2/teams), binds the one permitted team there is or asks the person, and checks any typed team against Vercel's own list and the binding. The token and its single-use refresh token stay in one custody record under the connection; the Vercel Connect management leg can use that record in place of a pasted token through a lease that names the record, never copies the value, is refused for another person or another team, and is never given to the workload leg.

supportEvidence.notes: Connect, approve, choose an account and role, invoke and the refusals, through the real command service over the persistent state ports against the loopback IAM Identity Center double (tests/connectors/doubles/aws-identity-center.ts), which checks each request independently.
Role credential renewal, access token refresh, session end, reconnect, and local and upstream disconnect against the same loopback double.
A sweep of every surface a caller can read for the secrets the double issued, with a positive control that finds them in custody.

Connect, approve, choose a team, invoke and the refusals, through the real command service over the persistent state ports against the loopback Vercel account double (tests/connectors/doubles/vercel-account.ts), which checks each request independently.
Refresh with a rotating single-use refresh token, session end, reconnect, a different person on reconnect, and local and upstream disconnect against the same loopback double.
A sweep of every surface a caller can read for the secrets and the email address the double issued, with a positive control that finds the secrets in custody.

The Vercel Connect management leg administering with a signed-in account's token against the loopback Connect double, which asks the account double whether a token is live; Connect's acceptance of such a token is modelled, not observed.

verified: RegisterClient: POST /client/register with clientName, clientType (public only), grantTypes, scopes; response clientId, clientSecret, clientIdIssuedAt, clientSecretExpiresAt, authorizationEndpoint, tokenEndpoint
StartDeviceAuthorization: POST /device_authorization with clientId, clientSecret, startUrl; response deviceCode, userCode, verificationUri, verificationUriComplete, expiresIn, interval
CreateToken: POST /token with clientId, clientSecret, grantType (device_code, refresh_token, authorization_code), deviceCode, refreshToken; response accessToken, tokenType, expiresIn, refreshToken

OIDC errors: JSON {error, error_description}; authorization_pending, slow_down, expired_token, access_denied, invalid_grant and invalid_request are HTTP 400, invalid_client is 401, server_error is 500

Portal operations: GET /assignment/accounts, GET /assignment/roles?account_id, GET /federation/credentials?account_id&role_name and POST /logout, each with the x-amz-sso_bearer_token header; max_result 1 to 100 with next_token paging; 400, 401, 404 and 429 documented
RoleCredentials members accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken, expiration; AccountInfo accountId, accountName, emailAddress; RoleInfo accountId, roleName
Logout leaves IAM role sessions created from the permission set running for their configured duration
Role session duration is one to twelve hours with a one hour default

Discovery at https://vercel.com/.well-known/openid-configuration: issuer https://vercel.com; device_authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, revocation_endpoint, registration_endpoint on https://api.vercel.com/login/oauth/; grant_types_supported includes urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code and refresh_token; scopes openid, email, profile, offline_access
vercel login uses the OAuth 2.0 Device Flow (changelog, September 12, 2025)
Access token vca_ valid one hour; refresh token vcr_ valid thirty days, single use, rotated on exchange, issued with offline_access
Client authentication `none` is offered per application for CLIs and public clients
GET /v2/user answers {user: {id, username, name, email, defaultTeamId, ...}}; GET /v2/teams takes limit, since, until and answers {teams: [{id, slug, name, ...}], pagination: {count, next, prev}}
unverified: The unit of RoleCredentials.expiration (the adapter reads epoch milliseconds and refuses a value that is not a role session)
The unit of clientSecretExpiresAt (read as epoch seconds)
That slow_down grows the interval by five seconds
Which error answers a wrong, foreign or already-used deviceCode (read as invalid_grant)
That an unassigned role or account is answered 404

That a refresh token is issued only to a client registered with the refresh_token grant and a scope, and that it is single use and rotated on use (the CreateToken page says only that a refreshToken is returned if present; the adapter never presents a token twice, whichever way the service behaves)

That a portal call with a lapsed token is answered 401. That another client's token is refused is the double's own rule and is in tension with the OIDC Welcome page (the tokens grant access to all of a person's account entitlements, not a particular application), so it is not relied on
The device authorization endpoint's request and response bodies and the verification page

That an application made on the Sign in with Vercel page may use the device grant, and that a `none` client is accepted at the device and token endpoints although the discovery document lists no such method
The error codes for a replayed device code and a replayed refresh token (read as invalid_grant) and the slow_down step (five seconds, RFC 8628)
That GET /v2/teams pages by `until` set to pagination.next, with `until` inclusive and next the last team's createdAt minus one
That GET /v2/user and GET /v2/teams answer their full forms to a token that holds only identity scopes (the REST reference documents `limited: true` forms the adapter's schemas do not model)

That an application the user removed answers 401 on the REST reads, that an unknown scope is invalid_scope at the device endpoint, and that an application restricted to a team is refused access_denied at refresh
That Vercel Connect accepts a device-grant access token on its management endpoints
